subject: Streamline Integrations – Template consolidation & redline decisions
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@streamline.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@streamline.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed partner MSA + SOW redlines (Streamline <> Redwood)

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday — excited to move forward. Attached are the initial redlines from our legal team: a marked-up MSA and a short SOW appendix that reflects the phased connector delivery. High level: we kept liability limits aligned to typical marketplace integrations but requested a tighter DPA section around telemetry retention and subprocessors.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can accept the subprocessor list and the 90-day telemetry retention ask? Also attaching the SOW for milestone acceptance criteria. If you prefer, we can drop in tracked changes into your template — happy to converge.

Attachments: Streamline_Redlines_v3.pdf, SOW_Appendix_v2.xlsx

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Partnerships, Streamline.ai
liam@streamline.ai
Attachment: Streamline_Redlines_v3.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: SOW_Appendix_v2.xlsx (Excel)

From: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed partner MSA + SOW redlines (Streamline <> Redwood)

Forwarding Streamline's redlines — please review and advise on the items below before I respond:

1) DPA/telemetry retention: they ask 90-day retention for telemetry logs that reference request metadata. Karthik — is that compliant with our current retention profiles for private deployments and hosted API?
2) Subprocessors list: they've shared a short list. Legal preference is to require 30-day notice and opt-out for specific subprocessors. Can we accommodate operationally?
3) SLA & liability caps: they lowered liability cap to 2x fees; they want consumer-friendly acceptance criteria in SOW for the connector. Ben — will that shape our ops SLOs or delivery timeline?

If we can agree on a concise set of counter-positions, I'll consolidate and send Streamline a single redline set (no back-and-forth).

Thanks — Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Streamline_Redlines_v3.pdf (from partner)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed partner MSA + SOW redlines (Streamline <> Redwood)

Maya / Ben — quick reads from legal ops:

- Telemetry retention: 90 days is okay for non-PII telemetry if it is scoped and hashed. We should explicitly exclude request/response content from that retention window. Propose: accept 90-day metadata retention but add clause: "no customer payload stored beyond 7 days unless explicitly opted by customer."
- Subprocessors: standard approach — accept their list but include requirement for 30-day notice and a right to object for material changes. We'll keep the right to require subprocessors to sign Redwood NDA addenda.
- Liability: 2x fees is low for platform risk. Propose counter: 5x fees or $2M cap (whichever is lower) for connector integrations; escalate if there is regulated-data processing.
- SOW acceptance criteria: make acceptance tied to automated integration tests + a 2-week operational validation window. This prevents ambiguous "accepted" language.

I'll draft short redline bullets you can include. No need to involve outside counsel yet unless they push on the $ cap.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed partner MSA + SOW redlines (Streamline <> Redwood)

Looping in ops notes:

- Delivery: the SOW's milestones are reasonable, but the acceptance tests will require collaboration on test harness (Streamline needs to provide an integration sandbox with sample payloads). That increases dev time by ~2 weeks. Capable to meet on our standard delivery timeline if they commit to sandbox + API keys by the first week.
- Support & SLA: if we accept a 90-day telemetry retention for metadata, we should add a clause that telemetry data used for debugging will be redacted and accessed only by named engineers. Also recommend adding a runbook handoff as a Milestone 3 deliverable.
- Commercial: liability cap change will materially affect our risk model — marketing is fine but finance will expect a pricing uplift. If legal pushes to 2x fees, request a 10% uplift in first-year partner margin.

Recommend: agree to metadata retention (with explicit payload exclusion), accept subprocessor notice with objection window, push liability cap to our proposed 5x fees/$2M, and nail down sandbox deliverables in SOW.

-Ben
Director, Partner Operations | Redwood Inference

From: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@streamline.ai>, contracts@streamline.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed partner MSA + SOW redlines (Streamline <> Redwood)

Hi Liam — thanks for sending these over and for the clear SOW appendix. We've consolidated internal feedback and attached a single counter-redline PDF. High-level summary below so it's easy for your team: 

1) Telemetry / DPA: Redwood can accept a 90-day retention for non-payload telemetry (request metadata, error traces) provided we explicitly exclude request/response content and apply hashing/redaction. We will add a clause limiting use to debugging and operations, with a named-engineer access control.
2) Subprocessors: Acceptable — we request 30-day notice of new subprocessors and a right to object for material changes. Subprocessors must sign an NDA addendum.
3) Liability cap: We cannot accept 2x fees. Proposed counter: 5x fees capped at $2,000,000. If Streamline requires a lower cap, we'll need a commercial uplift (we've flagged this to finance).
4) SOW acceptance: We'll make acceptance conditional on automated integration tests and a 2-week operational validation window. Streamline to provide an integration sandbox + sample payloads within five business days of countersignature.

Next steps: please review the attached consolidated redlines (PDF). If agreeable, we can issue a DocuSign envelope (link below) with the counter and proposed SOW appendix. If Streamline prefers, we can also accept tracked-changes on Redwood's MSA template — whichever speeds execution.

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/recipient?envelopeId=5f4a2b8c
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/8391 (DEAL-8391-STRM)

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up quickly.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan
